title: Beat the 4-cycle lower bound for cube-free graphs
premise_risks: Statement is a one-sided target; the vetter may prefer the full Θ(n^{8/5}) conjecture
Erdős conjectured the n^{8/5} order, but the problem is not commonly named after a person ('Turán number of the cube'); the stated target (beat n^{3/2}) is an unnamed sub-question
plain: How many edges can an n-vertex graph have without containing the 3-dimensional cube Q3 (8 vertices, 12 edges)? Erdos and Simonovits proved about n^{8/5} is an upper bound, but the best lower bound is still about n^{3/2}, from graphs with no 4-cycle at all (every 4-cycle-free graph is cube-free). Find cube-free graphs with polynomially more edges than that, or show that no such graphs exist.
math: Let $\mathrm{ex}(n,Q_3)$ be the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex simple graph with no subgraph isomorphic to the cube $Q_3$. Known: $(\tfrac12+o(1))n^{3/2}\le \mathrm{ex}(n,Q_3)= O(n^{8/5})$. Decide whether $\liminf_{n\to\infty}\dfrac{\log \mathrm{ex}(n,Q_3)}{\log n}>\dfrac32$, i.e. whether there is $\varepsilon>0$ with $\mathrm{ex}(n,Q_3)\ge n^{3/2+\varepsilon}$ for all large $n$. (Erdos conjectured the stronger $\mathrm{ex}(n,Q_3)=\Theta(n^{8/5})$.)
review_note: Known: Upper: Erdős–Simonovits (1970) O(n^{8/5}); new proof by Pinchasi–Sharir and Füredi (arXiv 1307.1062). Lower: Ω(n^{3/2}) from C4-free polarity graphs, since C4 ⊂ Q3 (Erdős problems page states no better lower bound known). Janzer–Sudakov (Forum Math. Sigma, arXiv 2211.02015): ex(n,Q_d)=O(n^{2-1/(d-1)+1/((d-1)2^{d-1})}), and they record that for Q3 the bounds n^{3/2} and n^{8/5} still stand.
